newsitem.title: USA: PrimeTime 24 says sues over DBS TV signals.
newsitem.headline: PrimeTime 24 says sues over DBS TV signals.

text.p: PrimeTime 24, a wholesaler of broadcast signals to satellite-TV companies, said on Friday that it filed suit against the major broadcast networks, the National Association of Broadcasters, and several TV affiliates.
The company charged in a suit filed in U.S. district court here that the networks and the others "have conspired illegally to stifle competition from the satellite broadcast industry."
PrimeTime said that under the Satellite Home Viewer Act it was permitted to sell the television signals. It said it sells the signals to three direct broadcast service companies.
It said that the networks and affiliates were seeking to put PrimeTime out of business. PrimeTime 24 is a unit of Great Universal American Industries.

"PrimeTime 24's lawsuit is absolutely without merit," said Edward Fritts, president of the National Association of Broadcaster in a statement. "It represents a sorry attempt at diverting attention from the fact that PrimeTime 24 is being sued in three federal courts for violating copyright laws under the Satellite Home Viewer Act."
NBC is a unit of General Electric Co, ABC is owned by Walt Disney Co, CBS is a part of Westinghouse Electric Corp, and Fox is owned by News Corp.
